title: Old Faithful

data.source: Old Faithful eruption lengths and waits, Azzalini and Bowman (1990), via the R datasets package (Rdatasets copy)

prediction: A line fitted on the first 136 eruptions predicts the wait from the last eruption's length with RMSE under 0.6 times the running mean's (P1); and the seed rule beats both the running mean and persistence (P2).
baseline: Running mean of earlier waits, persistence, and the rangers' recharge rule (which is P1 itself).
why: The wait is set by how much the last eruption emptied, which is the count idea. But that is exactly the recharge rule the rangers already use. The seed rule added nothing: it did not beat the plain running mean.
